character.name: Orren of the Lower Stair
character.story_function: Teach the player to expect one particular person before the game asks what that expectation was worth.

stages.title: A Lantern at the Lower Stair
stages.body:
A green lantern flickers beside a broken stair. Orren, a vault-runner with a silver map case, raises one hand before the party reaches for steel.

"The Anchor rearranges the floors when it feels watched," he says. "Let me mark one truth before it lies again."

stages.title: Someone Else's Weight
stages.body:
Orren is kneeling beside a stranger whose leg is bound with a torn map. His silver case is open on the stone. The safe route is already marked.

"I can carry him or the case," Orren says. "Not both. You do not owe me either."
stages.footer: He does not ask you to stay.

choices.label: Stay. We carry him together.  [MOVE -1 THIS DESCENT]

stages.title: One Minute
stages.body:
The next time Orren finds you, nobody is bleeding. Nobody is chasing him. He has made tea over a flame too small to warm the stair.

"It tastes terrible," he says. "Sit anyway."

He tells you he was born near a sea he barely remembers. He keeps drawing coastlines into maps that do not need them.

stages.title: The Door That Opens Backward
stages.body:
Orren is waiting before you see the green lantern. He has started doing that now.

He corrects one of his own marks, complains that Sera's tea is worse than his, and folds the map before you can ask where the new line goes.

"Next time," he says. "I will show you the door that opens backward."
stages.footer: He says next time as though next time is a place.

choices.label: Tell him you will look for the lantern.

stages.title: The Empty Stair
stages.body:
The stair is there. The green lantern is not.

Orren's silver map case rests against the wall, closed. A fresh route line stops halfway through a mark. There is no blood. No body. No departure sign. Nothing in the room explains why the room feels wrong.
stages.footer: You knew where he was supposed to be.

stages.title: Someone Else's Mark
stages.body:
Another traveler has copied one of Orren's old marks onto the wall. The angle is wrong. You notice immediately.

The route still works.
stages.footer: A useful thing can outlive the person who made it. That is not the same as the person remaining.
